# parsec v5 — baseline arm `v5_b1_e1`

**Spec:** none — this arm characterises a rebuilt benchmark rather than testing a new optimizer design (see "Why v5 exists")
**Agent model:** `claude-sonnet-4-6`
**Optimizer model:** none — **no optimization step.** There is no seed/candidate/best/final lineage here, unlike [`v4_t_e1`](../../v4/v4_t_e1/summary.md) and [`v4_g_e1`](../../v4/v4_g_e1/summary.md)
**Budget:** `num_trials: 5, max_iterations: 0, max_usd: 50.0` per task (no optimizer budget — none was spent)
**Ledger:** [`results.json`](results.json), generated by [`../../../scripts/build_v5_b1_results_json.py`](../../../scripts/build_v5_b1_results_json.py) from the frozen, per-trial-audited [`source_v5_b1_e1.json`](source_v5_b1_e1.json)
**Heatmap:** [`../../../ui/heatmap_v5_b1_e1.html`](../../../ui/heatmap_v5_b1_e1.html) · **per-trial view:** [`../../../ui/trials_v5_b1_e1.html`](../../../ui/trials_v5_b1_e1.html)
**Recipes:** [`../../../recipes/v5/v5_b1_e1/`](../../../recipes/v5/v5_b1_e1/)
**Artifacts:** [`../../../artifacts/v5/seed/`](../../../artifacts/v5/seed/) — one shared bundle, the original skill, identical across all 136 tasks
**Per-task reports:** [`../../../reports/v5/v5_b1_e1/`](../../../reports/v5/v5_b1_e1/) (`<task>.md`, 136 files)
**Cost/time:** [`cost_time/`](cost_time/) (`v5_b1_e1_results_table.md`)
**Benchmark quality review:** [`../../../reports/v5-benchmark-quality-review.md`](../../../reports/v5-benchmark-quality-review.md) — grader defects found in this arm's trials

## The one-line result

**Mean reward 0.8114** across all 136 tasks, from 679 of 680 trials after a
per-trial audit. On the 34 tasks carried over from v4 unchanged, v5 reproduces v4's own original-skill
baseline to **-0.002** on average (SE 0.018) — the strongest
evidence available that the rebuilt benchmark, the pinned skill and the audited data are sound.

## Why v5 exists, and what this arm's skill actually is

v4's 34-task set and h4's 30-task held-out set had both drifted from the copies this branch's own v4/h4
tables were built against. Rather than reconcile that lineage, v5 is a from-scratch rebuild: new task
copies under a `bench-v5-` prefix, no shared content with any v4/h4 tree, pooling two independently
authored 68-task drops into **136 tasks**.

This arm's skill is **verified byte-identical (8/8 prompt files) to parsec commit `28e2c40`'s
`config/prompts/`**, checked against a fresh clone of the parsec reference repo, and equally
byte-identical to this branch's own [`artifacts/v4/seed/`](../../../artifacts/v4/seed/).

> **A previous run of this sweep was discarded.** `v5_t1_e1` (68 tasks, PR #801) ran a skill
> byte-identical to [`artifacts/v4/v4_g_e1/rejected/cand_0001`](../../../artifacts/v4/v4_g_e1/rejected/cand_0001)
> — a candidate from v4's **global optimizer** arm, left installed in the live parsec clone's working
> tree (parsec's git HEAD still read `28e2c40`, so `git status` would not have shown it) and inherited
> when the v5 tree was built from that clone. It was never a baseline. **Pin the artifact under test to
> a known commit and verify it by bytes**, rather than copying whatever a live working tree holds.
>
> The shared parsec-live tree in the intake worktree still holds `cand_0001`; this arm was not affected,
> because the adapter writes the skill under test into each lane's own `config/prompts/` and parsec-live
> reads the lane's directory (verified by reproducing its import inside a lane). Seventeen lanes hold
> `cand_0001` *now* only because the adapter's restore step copied the lane's starting contents back
> after evaluation; the trials were served the pristine skill, and those tasks score like it
> (`cloud-024-guid-to-account` = 0.200, exactly v4's pristine seed value).

## Data quality: a per-trial audit, and what it caught

The first collection of this sweep reported **0 errored trials — and was wrong.** A per-trial audit of
every trial's on-disk record (harbor `result.json`, verifier `reward-detail.json`, agent transcript,
trial log) found **74 of 680 trials (11%) dead**, all scored as genuine 0.0:

| failure | trials | cause |
|---|--:|---|
| `AgentTimeoutError` | 68 | **0 tool calls** in the 600–900s budget: the agent never got its first LLM response. Clustered in time (11–20% of trials 14:00–19:00, 0–4% after) — a gateway degradation window |
| port collision | 5 | on host `cccxc434` port 8000 was already held, so that lane's parsec-live never started; every request 404'd (`cloud-304`, which had looked like a "deterministic zero") |
| gateway budget cap | 1 | `429 Budget has been exceeded` |

cap-evolve counts only exceptions it catches itself, so all 74 reached the ledger as clean zeros. The
44 affected tasks were re-run in full; the one dead trial that recurred (`platform-113`, which hung
on its first LLM call in three separate runs) is excluded, leaving that task at n=4 with an
`audit_note`. Twice, that hang also left a simulator tool call in flight, and the next trials'
seed installs were then refused (`HTTP 409 ... in-flight tool call`) — a cascade worth guarding against
in the optimizer arms, which run far more trials per lane. The generator refuses to build if any task has errored trials without an audit note or
fewer than 4 valid ones.

**What the audit also confirmed clean:** 0 seed-install errors; rollout reward equal to verifier
reward on every trial; agent model `claude-sonnet-4-6` in all 136 lanes; the two task sets'
`verify.py` logically identical (they differ only in a v4→v5 rename). The 26 trials that made no
tool call are genuine original-skill behaviour — answering a bare identifier with "could you
clarify", or wrongly claiming it has no Icinga/Marketplace access — the routing gaps `cand_0001` had
patched.

**Why it matters for the comparison:** the dead trials were not spread evenly. The queue ran
alphabetically, so 69% of 10-10's trials fell in the degraded window versus 47% of 10-12's. That,
not the tasks, produced the large difference in spread between the sets that the first collection
showed (0.699 vs 0.394, which became 0.236 vs 0.228 once the dead trials were re-run).

## v5 vs v4: same tasks, same skill, same result

v4's original-skill baselines are `v4_t1_e1` ("our_baseline", n=3) and JB's external `baseline-v2`
(n=1), from [`../../v4/v4_t_e1/results.json`](../../v4/v4_t_e1/results.json). Not `v4_t4_e*` —
those are the static merge of 21 *optimized* bundles. On the 34 tasks v5 carried over from v4, the
instructions are unchanged (0/34) and so are the contracts (1/34); seed edits are a median of 1 line.

|  | JB `baseline-v2` (n=1) | v4 `v4_t1_e1` (n=3) | **v5 `v5_b1_e1`** (n=5) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| mean, 34 tasks | 0.821 | 0.838 | **0.836** |
| regression (30) | 0.833 | 0.845 | 0.843 |
| challenge (4) | 0.730 | 0.792 | 0.789 |

Paired per-task difference v5 − v4_t1: **-0.0019** (sd 0.103,
SE 0.0177); only 1 task moves by more than 0.25. The four largest moves:
`icinga-014-check-script-path-moved` (0.883 → 0.515), `platform-001-ee-entrypoint-rca` (0.713 → 0.480), `platform-032-shared-secret-not-a-registry-outage` (0.650 → 0.880), `platform-005-wrong-owner-trap` (0.813 → 1.000). `icinga-014` is the one worth a look.

**h4 does not compare.** The 21 v5 tasks that share an id with h4's held-out set were all rewritten
going into v5 — every instruction (median 10 lines), every contract (median 294 lines), the seeds
(median 101 lines) and the verifier. v5 scores them at 0.922 against h4's 0.72–0.74; that gap is
the rewrite, not the skill. They are labelled `h4-rewritten` in the ledger and h4's numbers are
deliberately not carried into any v5 table.

## The two task sets

| metric | 10-10 (68) | 10-12 (68) | all (136) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| mean reward | 0.8482 | 0.7745 | 0.8114 |
| median | 0.9685 | 0.8215 | 0.8696 |
| sd across tasks | 0.2274 | 0.2154 | 0.2238 |
| saturated | 32 | 12 | 44 |
| unsaturated | 36 | 56 | 92 |
| mean of unsaturated | 0.7133 | 0.7262 | 0.7211 |
| zero-mean tasks | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| variable-reward tasks | 28 | 48 | 76 |
| variable % | 41.2 | 70.6 | 55.9 |
| deterministic | 40 | 20 | 60 |
| mean spread (variable only) | 0.236 | 0.228 | 0.231 |
| mean sd (variable only) | 0.096 | 0.088 | 0.091 |
| mean sd (all tasks) | 0.039 | 0.062 | 0.051 |

10-10 minus 10-12: **+0.0737**, SE 0.0380, t = 1.94, two-sided
permutation p = **0.06** — borderline, not negligible. About half of it is
composition: 10-10 contains the 21 rewritten h4 tasks, which the original skill now finds easy; without
them the gap is +0.0406.

| origin | set | n | mean | median | saturated | what it is |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `v4-34` | 10-10 | 34 | 0.8365 | 0.9380 | 13 | v4's original 34 tasks; contracts unchanged |
| `h4-rewritten` | 10-10 | 21 | 0.9224 | 1.0000 | 13 | shares an h4 id; instruction, contract, seeds and verifier all rewritten |
| `renamed-content-changed` | 10-10 | 2 | 0.5350 | 0.5350 | 0 | kept a v4/h4 number, content changed |
| `new-10-10` | 10-10 | 11 | 0.7998 | 1.0000 | 6 | new in the first drop |
| `new-10-12` | 10-12 | 68 | 0.7745 | 0.8215 | 12 | the whole second drop |

That composition is also what puts 10-10's median at 0.9685: the h4-rewritten
subset has a median of 1.0, with 13 of 21 tasks saturated. 10-12 is genuinely less saturated and
varies more often — its contracts carry more gradable items per task (4.6 vs 3.9), so partial credit
is commoner — while the spread *when* a task varies is the same in both sets.

**Consequence for the train/test split:** stratify `o5`/`h5` by task set and category rather than
splitting purely at random, so neither half inherits more of the easy h4-rewritten subset or more of
10-12's partial-credit texture.

## Stochasticity, and the noise floor it sets

**76 of 136 tasks (55.9%) return a different reward across
identical repeated trials**, but the variation is small: mean per-task trial sd 0.051,
0.091 among the variable tasks alone.

| quantity | value | what it bounds |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean per-task trial sd | 0.0508 | raw run-to-run noise |
| SE of a 5-trial task mean | 0.0227 | one task's score |
| 95% CI half-width, per task | 0.0445 | per-task claims |
| **min detectable per-task delta** | **~0.09** | one task's before/after at n=5 |
| SE of the 136-task suite mean | 0.0192 | suite-level claims |

A per-task change smaller than about **0.09** is indistinguishable
from noise at 5 trials; the suite mean is resolved to ~0.02. Per-task gating is
workable for the optimizer arms, provided the gate requires a margin of that size rather than any gain.

*(The first collection put these at 0.145 sd and ~0.25 — nearly three times too pessimistic, all of it
from the dead-trial zeros.)*

## Data-quality notes

1. **One task is n=4** (`platform-113-account-region-override-not-capacity`); every other task has 5
   valid trials.
2. **One genuine zero.** `icinga-072-alert-output-not-decoy-metrics` scores 0.0 on every trial with no
   infra error: asked about an Icinga alert, the original skill routes to the OCP-V agent to check worker
   capacity (the decoy) and never queries Icinga. A real routing trap, and a valid task.
3. **Grader defects.** Several tasks penalise correct answers — a forbidden-phrase matcher with no
   negation handling ("In Downtime: **No**" fails a "never say *in downtime*" check), an RCA verdict
   requiring a taxonomy word the agent is never shown, and over-literal tool-argument matching. These are
   properties of the authored benchmark, not of this run; see
   [`../../../reports/v5-benchmark-quality-review.md`](../../../reports/v5-benchmark-quality-review.md).
   They matter more for the optimizer arms than for this baseline.

## Next moves

- Decide, per the quality review, whether to patch the grader defects in v5's copy or exclude those
  tasks from the split.
- Split the 136 into `o5` (train) and `h5` (held-out), **stratified by task set and category**.
- Run the task-by-task (`t`) and global (`g`) optimizer arms on `o5`, validate on `h5` — with a
  per-task acceptance margin of about 0.09, and the per-trial audit
  run before any number is trusted.
